Coverage is the rendered roster (Stop, TeammateIdle, the yield-tool matcher): a yield primitive outside that roster is uncovered, reconciled when the toolchain register changes. The dispatch ledger sees only hooked launch tools, so a task launched through an unhooked tool costs one spurious deny and a dead task read as live permits one idle until staleness catches it, both directions bounded and logged. An open or proposed id that vanishes from the enumeration without a closed receipt, OR (FIX 2) a previously-actionable id DEMOTED to proposed/ungranted without a closed receipt (the checkpoint records each id's eligibility for this), is injected as a cannot-evaluate by the anti-shrinkage checkpoint (backlog-checkpoint.json: the first window has no union to compare, and a drop forced by the checkpoint's id bound is logged to guard-events, a failed append warned about in the hook's output, so a drop is never silent; a checkpoint or init marker that cannot be written is named in the hook's output whether or not its guard-events row is written, and an unwritten checkpoint does not record that window's items, so one that then vanishes or is demoted before a later checkpoint write succeeds is not held as such unless an earlier checkpoint records it); that eligibility memory is itself in the actor-writable state dir, the same categorical residual. A bound-released ALLOW WITH FINDINGS past ANY non-closed disposition (actionable, cannot-evaluate, waiting, blocked, or proposed) is marked forced_unresolved (a guard-events row plus an append-only row in forced-exit.jsonl, each normally raised once, at least once if recording it in forced-exit-surfaced.json fails, a failed append of either surfacing in the warn banner itself) and is triaged by the next resume audit; no register row, attestation, or escape-adjacent artefact suppresses that record.

AIRTIGHT-NARROW (L11 redesign: the GD-112 philosophy applied to diff-dumps). NO-ASK posture: this guard never returns an ask; read every ASK/ASKS/OVER-ASK below as its no-ask resolution, an ALLOW with an informational note for an unproven producer-capable form (a console-readability convention, not a hazard), while a CONFIRMED console patch that fits no proof DENIES-and-educates (use --stat or a redirect/pager). A best-effort QUOTE/REDIRECT-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command via the shared raw-command tokenizer (_lex_command), which decides quoting and REDIRECTION from raw character positions BEFORE tokenizing, so a redirection ANYWHERE in a command (leading, interspersed, or trailing) is recorded as metadata and REMOVED from the argv, closing the redirect-pollution class shared across the lexical Bash hooks. An unquoted # at a word boundary is a COMMENT (the rest of the line is ignored, so a redirect or pipe that is commented out earns no proof; a mid-word # such as ticket#123 stays literal); a backslash-newline is a LINE CONTINUATION that joins (comment handling is RE-APPLIED at the word boundary a continuation exposes, so git diff <backslash-newline># > out.txt still comments out the redirect, while a continuation that lands MID-word keeps a following # literal) and never injects a synthetic empty argv element (which would have mis-set the subcommand and defeated the sibling guards); and a redirect target is classified CONSERVATIVELY on BOTH its raw and its LEXICALLY-normalized form (os.path.normpath, never touching the filesystem): a target whose RAW form begins with /dev or /proc is treated as a device and DENIED even if a .. in it would normalize elsewhere (git diff > /dev/../tmp/out.txt DENIES, an over-block in the SAFE direction), an ABSOLUTE target that NORMALIZES to under /dev or /proc is an unambiguous console/device target and DENIES (git diff > /tmp/../dev/stdout), a RELATIVE target whose normalized FIRST component is dev or proc (git diff > dev/stdout, > ./dev/stdout, > proc/self/fd/1) is CWD-DEPENDENT - from cwd / or via a dev/proc symlink it IS that device, but from an ordinary working tree it is a plain relative file - so it cannot be proven a plain file and ASKS (opaque), never a silent ALLOW and never a hard DENY of a legitimate write into a dev/ or proc/ subdirectory of the working tree itself, a .. in a target NOT under /dev or /proc yields an OPAQUE target that cannot be proven a plain file and ASKS (git diff > /tmp/../out.txt), and a plain static non-/dev,/proc file target ALLOWS (git diff > /tmp/out.txt); a relative .. escape that normpath cannot resolve (../../../dev/stdout) is likewise opaque rather than a proven real file. Rather than ENUMERATE every dumping form of git (an unbounded shell + git-option grammar, GD-34/F-119), the ALLOW path PROVES the safe form: a git diff-PRODUCER is ALLOWED only when the WHOLE command matches one of SIX closed proofs. (A) EXACT help: a metacharacter-free git <producer> --help or -h (and the exact git stash show --help/-h). (B) EXACT summary-only: a metacharacter-free single simple command (a conservative character set of letters, digits, space, tab, and _ - . / = : @ , + % and no shell reserved word), whose first resolved words are literally git and a summary-capable producer (diff/show/range-diff/log/diff-tree/diff-index/diff-files, plus the explicit git stash show), carrying at least one EXACT summary selector (--stat/--shortstat/--numstat/--name-only/--name-status) before a --/--end-of-options boundary and no other option-like word before the boundary except an exact --no-patch (bare operands allowed). (C) DIRECT static real-file diversion: a SINGLE simple command whose command word is literally git, a possible producer, with no opaque shell feature, whose FINAL stdout redirect (last-redirect-wins over the raw redirect metadata) is proven to land on a static non-/dev,/proc file - supporting leading, interspersed, and trailing redirects, but never a dynamic target (a variable, command substitution, or tilde), a descriptor duplication (1>&2, or a 3>out 1>&3 fd-graph, classified opaque), or a /dev,/proc target. (D) EXACT terminal pager pipeline: a plain literal unwrapped git producer, an exact | (not |&), then exactly one bare pager word (less/more/most/pager) with no options, operands, or redirection and no later pipe. (E) BENIGN git log listing: a metacharacter-free single simple command whose first words are literally git and log, every option before a --/--end-of-options boundary drawn from an EXACT allowlist of VALUE-FREE, provably-diff-free display/traversal flags (--oneline, --graph, --decorate, --no-decorate, --abbrev-commit, --reverse, --all) with bare revision/pathspec operands allowed - a plain commit listing that provably emits no diff (git log renders a patch ONLY with a patch flag, and a summary --stat form is already proof B). A git log carrying ANY other flag - a patch flag, a pickaxe -G/-S (whose diff output depends on a co-present -p), a summary/file-list flag (--numstat/--shortstat/--name-only/--name-status, which are the proof-B summary escape, allowed there like git diff --name-only), a value-taking option such as --format/-n <count>/--author=/--since=/--grep=, or any unknown flag - is NOT admitted by proof E and routes to the default (ASK, or DENY on a confirmed patch). (F) EXACT git show BLOB READ: a metacharacter-free single simple command whose first resolved words are literally git and show and whose FIRST non-option argument after show is a BLOB SELECTOR (a non-option token containing a colon, the <ref>:<path> or :<path> form). In that form git show prints ONE file contents at a revision - no diff, no @@ hunk headers, no +/- lines - so it is cat against a revision (the normal way to read a file on an un-checked-out branch) and renders no console diff. A bare git show <commit> (no colon-bearing first operand) is NOT this proof and stays covered (ASK, or DENY on a confirmed patch); a compound or redirected form is outside the single-simple-command proof and ASKS. This is a best-effort lexical heuristic (a separated option value containing a colon is a disclosed residual, erring toward reading a file, never toward a false diff-dump deny). The ALLOW path DELIBERATELY does NOT parse the full git/shell option grammar. Every OTHER possible producer is ASK or DENY: a producer CONFIRMED to emit a console patch (a default diff/range-diff, a default git show that is NOT the blob-read form, a patch-flagged listing, a summary token in a NON-option position such as git diff -- --stat, a producer piped into a known console/truncating sink cat/tee/head/tail, or a stdout redirect to /dev,/proc) and fitting no proof DENIES; any other producer-capable-but-unproven form ASKS. A producer that diverts its output with --output/-o writes the diff to THAT target, not stdout, so a shell redirect or a pager is a DECOY: proofs C and D do not apply, a --output to a /dev,/proc console DENIES, and a --output to a file or a dynamic target ASKS. A command word this guard cannot resolve to a literal git (an ANSI-C dollar-single-quote form or a $VAR expansion) beside a producer surface is never proven benign and never a CONFIRMED console dump: it ASKS. Across a compound or multiple producers, DENY outranks ASK, and a multi-command form is NEVER allowed merely because one segment is safe. The possible-producer scope is BROAD (a git word followed by a producer surface in the cleaned argv, robust to quote fragmentation, OR a raw-text probe that over-matches quoted prose), so it OVER-ASKS by design; on a tokenizer parse failure (an unbalanced quote or an unsupported construct such as a heredoc or process substitution) an apparent producer ASKS - never a silent allow, and no summary or redirect regex can earn an ALLOW from an unparseable command. DELIBERATE OVER-ASKS, disclosed: a wrapper (env/sudo/command git diff), a pathed git (/usr/bin/git show), a leading assignment, any quote in a would-be summary command, a git log carrying any extra or unknown flag OUTSIDE the proof-E benign set (git log -5, git log -G/-S, git log --format, git log --author=), git grep diff, an extra summary modifier (git diff -M --stat, git diff -S --stat, git diff --stat=80), a compound, and quoted prose (an echo of the literal text git diff) all ASK rather than risk a false ALLOW. HONEST non-catches (best-effort, not chased): a git alias, a shell function, or a PATH-shadow name that omits a detectable git word; an expansion, eval, base64, or nested-script text that defeats both the cleaned-token scan and the raw fallback marker; a producer subcommand outside the declared roster; a diff produced by a NON-git tool or assembled across commands, or emitted outside the Bash tool; runtime or config behaviour that writes directly to a tty (a pager or GIT_PAGER/config set in a PRIOR turn); a static path target that is itself a symlink, FIFO, or device node, or that resolves to one through a symlinked ANCESTOR directory (a relative first-component dev/proc NAME is now caught lexically and ASKS, but the check never resolves symlinks, so a device reached through ANY symlinked ancestor, whether or not that ancestor is named dev/proc, is not distinguished), or that races after the check; and pager or PATH resolution at runtime. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the common/accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it. DEADLINE: main() gives this check 8 seconds (the 10-second hook timeout less 2), counted from before its payload read, and fails closed with exit 2 when it has not decided by then; on the worst shapes the hooks self-test times, up to 1 MB, its slowest call took about 0.26 s in-process on a 24-core host with Python 3.14.4 (2026-10-15). Interpreter start-up and a wait the interpreter cannot interrupt (a read from a hung mount, a long call into C code) fall outside that deadline, and whether the platform blocks a call whose hook it stops at its own timeout is unverified. Where SIGALRM, setitimer or the main thread is unavailable, or SIGALRM is blocked, the check runs with no deadline; cleanup that runs while the deadline unwinds is outside it.

This Stop layer is a NON-BLOCKING surfacing WARN (systemMessage, exit 0), not a hard block: by Stop time the wall has already rendered, and because this layer keeps no loop bound of its own and does not read the stop_hook_active field of the Stop input, a hard block could wedge the session, so hard prevention lives in the PreToolUse diff-source layer instead. It catches only a unified-diff wall in the final assistant message of a turn: diff --git headers, paired @@ hunk headers, fenced diff/patch/udiff blocks (backtick or tilde) of 10 or more lines, and mixed +/- runs of 8 or more lines. It does not catch a diff dumped mid-turn between tool calls, side-by-side or word-diff renderings, or raw log or patch walls that carry none of those markers; a mixed +/- Markdown checklist can rarely trip the +/- run detector (accepted residual).

PREVIEW CHANNEL ONLY: a standalone file installed by hand from .preview/, not part of the pack's plugin, and off until AIQT_CONSTRAINT_RECORD names the project's durable record. After a compaction reported by the platform's own markers (SessionStart with source compact, or PreCompact), it reminds the assistant of the record's Constraint lines on every user prompt, and refuses the turn end, while the record holds no Constraints-reread entry dated after the compaction and no more than 60 seconds ahead of the hook's clock (an entry dated up to 60 seconds ahead counts); the refusals are capped at 3 in a row, after which each later stop is allowed with a warning and no entry, unless the host sends stop_hook_active false on a turn end that continues a refusal. A refusal whose count cannot be saved is allowed with a warning, also on a Stop whose stop_hook_active field is explicitly false. The refusal count is kept in the hook's state file, so the cap holds when the platform's stop_hook_active field is absent or true; the count is reset to 0 only by a UserPromptSubmit event, a new compaction, or a Stop whose stop_hook_active field is explicitly false, never by an allowed stop, so without UserPromptSubmit registered and without that field every later stop until the next compaction is allowed with the warning (a missed refusal), and a state file that cannot be parsed (an unknown count) has the same effect from its first Stop. An explicit false is trusted as a new turn, so a host that sends it on a Stop that continues a refusal is refused at every such Stop (the cap does not hold). It proves only that an entry was written, not that the record was read or a constraint honoured; it names only constraints written in the record; a compaction without one of those markers (a host without the events, a hook not registered for them, a new session) is not seen; with no state location or no session key in the payload a compaction is reminded once and then forgotten; if its state location exists but cannot be examined, it keeps reminding with the compaction time unknown (a reminder no entry can clear, which says so) and allows each turn end with a warning; a state file over its size limit is read as a compaction at the file's modification time; a state file deleted after a compaction forgets that compaction, so the reminder and the refusals stop silently; concurrent hook runs are serialized by a lock file beside the state file, and a call saves only while that lock file and the state file are the ones it locked and loaded: a call that cannot take the lock within 2 seconds saves nothing (a compaction not recorded, a count not reset) and allows a turn end it would refuse with a warning that names the lock, and a call whose lock file is deleted or replaced while it holds it (also one moved away and put back after another call saved), or whose state file another call saved meanwhile, saves nothing and allows a turn end it would refuse with a warning that the refusal count cannot be saved (a deletion, replacement or save that lands in the few system calls between its last check and its write can still let one stale save through, and so can a save whose state file matches the loaded one in device, inode, size, modification time and change time, all five fields it compares, as when an inode number is reused within the filesystem's timestamp granularity); while the lock cannot be taken at all (a lock path that is a symbolic link or not a regular file, a lock file it cannot open, a filesystem that refuses flock, a platform without flock), it keeps no state, so a compaction is reminded once and then forgotten and, with no compaction saved before then, every turn end passes silently (a missed reminder and a missed refusal), while a compaction saved before then is still reminded and each turn end is allowed with a warning; a state folder moved away or deleted during a session forgets the compaction silently, like a deleted state file; once a record is declared every call creates the state directory and an empty lock file for its session, and nothing removes the lock or state files; an entry beyond the first MiB of the record is not seen, and a line cut at that limit is dropped; and the host clock is trusted.

Registry-scoped: inert with no registry at the session cwd's git-resolved toplevel (no ancestor walk, unlike orch-truncation-guard; AIQT_ORCH_REQUIRE_REGISTRY is not read here), and an unreadable registry allows silently with no guard-events row. Blocks a blocking question ONLY when the declared operating-mode record reads as unattended (this guards one known mistake shape, a blocking prompt idling an unattended run; it is not a security boundary). The mode record fails CLOSED to that guards-armed (unattended) posture, so the question is denied, for every read of the mode path that ends in neither not found nor a decoded text, the deny naming the reason: a mode path holding a NUL character, or one that is not strict UTF-8 (a lone surrogate, which is also how a surrogate-escaped non-UTF-8 name arrives), refused fail-closed before any open even where the OS could open it; a file that cannot be opened or read (a permission error, a socket, whose non-blocking open itself fails (ENXIO on Linux), or a missing file under a parent path that is a regular file, whose open reports not a directory rather than not found); one that is not a regular file (a directory, a FIFO, or a device such as /dev/zero, refused by an fstat after the non-blocking open and before any read, so a FIFO with no writer does not wait); one larger than 1048576 bytes (the reader reads at most one byte more), or one whose bytes are not valid UTF-8; and, for the text read, in these cases: an Operating-mode: declaration whose value is empty or begins with neither attended nor unattended; or, with no declaration line, content that parses as JSON but is not exactly an object whose one key, mode, holds a string beginning with attended or unattended (a bare JSON scalar such as true, 42, null or a quoted string, an array, an object with other keys, or one whose mode is missing, not a string or unrecognized), or content beginning with {, [ or a double quote that does not parse as JSON (malformed, partial, trailing text, duplicate keys, or nesting too deep to parse). It fails OPEN, allowing the question, in these cases: no declared mode path, a file whose open reports not found, an empty or whitespace-only file, or content with no declaration line that does not parse as JSON and does not begin with {, [ or a double quote (prose, including prose beginning with a number or a word, such as 42 items done or true trailing); that fail-open is logged to guard-events (where that append fails, the call is still allowed, with a note saying the row could not be written). Every input ends in one of these answers or the attended allow below; only a stall the hook timeout bounds can delay it (a path lookup on a hung mount, a read from a stalled filesystem, or what a device driver's open does). An attended mode is allowed with no guard-events row. The deny instruction distinguishes record-and-continue for ordinary decisions from record-and-HOLD for anything at the human-oversight threshold; the hook redirects the question and never licenses acting without the answer. Each denied ask appends ONE idempotent machine row keyed on session_id plus tool_use_id, carrying a bounded redacted summary (question count, length, digest), never the question text, and a guard-events row; a failed guard-events append adds a short recording-failure warning to the deny reason and the banner while the deny stands. Its behaviour is verified by the behaviour self-test. It cannot see a blocking prompt raised outside the AskUserQuestion tool. DEADLINE: main() gives this check 8 seconds (the 10-second hook timeout less 2), counted from before its payload read, and fails closed with exit 2 when it has not decided by then; on the worst shapes the hooks self-test times, up to 1 MB, its slowest call took under 0.01 s in-process on a 24-core host with Python 3.14.4 (2026-10-15). Interpreter start-up and a wait the interpreter cannot interrupt (a read from a hung mount, a long call into C code) fall outside that deadline, and whether the platform blocks a call whose hook it stops at its own timeout is unverified. Where SIGALRM, setitimer or the main thread is unavailable, or SIGALRM is blocked, the check runs with no deadline; cleanup that runs while the deadline unwinds is outside it.

REGISTRY-SCOPED: entirely inert unless an orchestration registry (.aiqt/orchestration.local.json or .aiqt/orchestration.json) is present at the session cwd's git-resolved toplevel (no ancestor walk, unlike orch-truncation-guard; AIQT_ORCH_REQUIRE_REGISTRY is not read here) AND a declared orchestrator lease or mode record is live, so plain Q&A sessions and bounded workers never inherit the global backlog. FAIL-OPEN on its own I/O errors, none of which wedges the session: an unresolvable cwd, or an inactive or unreadable lease with no mode record read as declared, SILENTLY ALLOWS the stop (no warn banner, no guard-event); a DECLARED lease max_age_hours that is not usable (a boolean, zero, negative, NaN, infinite or a non-number) on an otherwise-live lease is a scope cannot-evaluate that DENIES through the same cannot-evaluate path as an unreadable item proof, never a silent guards-off (the loop bound and the operator escape release, a live mode record outranks it, and a session the lease does not name stays a non-holder; a CHANGE for adopters: the scope check previously read zero, a negative number, a non-number such as a string, false or NaN as no horizon, true as a one-hour horizon and infinity as a horizon never reached, so such a registry now denies the stop until the value is corrected to a positive finite number of hours), while a mode record the mode reader fails closed on counts as declared, so scope is live: one that cannot be opened (a socket included) or read, one that is not a regular file, one over its size bound, one whose bytes are not valid UTF-8, one at a path holding a NUL or not strict UTF-8, and one read as text whose declaration or JSON marker is malformed or unrecognized (an empty or unrecognized Operating-mode: value, or a JSON-shaped marker that does not parse or is not exactly a single string mode key); an unreadable registry ALLOWS with a warn banner but no guard-event; and a turn-state.json that cannot be read or does not hold a JSON object, or a stop_denials value in it that validation rejects (anything but a JSON integer from 0 to 9999, so a float such as 1.0, a boolean or a string), in a state directory the hook can search takes the bounded loop-bound exit, while a state directory the hook cannot search (owner modes 0000, 0200, 0400 and 0600; this and every other owner-mode list in this residue hold for a hook that runs without root as the state directory's owner and holds neither CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, which searches and writes the directory in every mode, nor CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, which searches it and reads turn-state.json in every mode, with the state directory on a filesystem mounted read-write and not marked immutable, since a read-only mount or an immutable directory fails every save) reads as a fresh turn-state, so a count already at the bound is not seen there and the stop is judged afresh (a deny there then allows with findings, because its denial counter cannot be saved). A deny whose denial counter cannot be saved fails open with findings. The save needs a state directory the hook can write and search, and read where the platform lacks O_PATH: opening the directory needs read permission on it only without O_PATH; after that open, the stat of turn-state.json, the creation of the save's temporary file, the replacement and, after a failed step, the removal of that temporary file each look a name up in it and so need search permission (the fchmod, write and fsync on the temporary file's descriptor look no name up), and the creation, the replacement and that removal also write to it (a temporary file left by a hook process killed mid-save stays, since no later save removes it). So of the eight owner modes of the state directory, a stop the decision core denies is blocked only in 0300 and 0700 with O_PATH and only in 0700 without it, and allows with findings in every other mode, a writable turn-state.json in a state directory the hook cannot write included (the earlier in-place overwrite let that deny stand). But (FIX 1) an enumerator error or timeout, and any cannot-evaluate (an unreadable proof source), FAIL CLOSED-CONTINUE: the stop is DENIED (ignorance refuses the wind-down), releasable by the operator-owned escape sentinel and never a clean close, bounded by the guard-owned loop bound past which it becomes a deliberate, recorded forced exit. Each deny appends a guard-events row; a failed append leaves no row and adds a short recording-failure warning to the block reason (exit 2 carries no banner) while the deny stands. The row of an ALLOW released by the operator escape is the only record that the override was used, so a failed append there adds a warning to the banner while the ALLOW stands; the row of a clean ALLOW with no escape is the over-fire metric only and best effort, a failed append there not reported. The deny is BOUNDED by two separate triggers, either of which ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS. The first is the guard-owned counter: stop_denials in turn-state.json, which the guard raises by one with each saved deny and which genuine human input resets, allows at most two saved denies per epoch, and works only where the state directory lets the hook read and save it (above). The second is the platform's own loop signal: the Claude Code hooks reference documents a stop_hook_active field in the Stop input, true when Claude Code is already continuing as a result of a stop hook, and a Stop whose payload carries it as the JSON value true takes the same exit whatever the count (a string value is not the signal); the guard only reads this field from the payload and never saves it, so it relieves whatever the mode of the state directory. The operator escape sentinel yields the clean ALLOW only when it passes enforced acceptance: a regular file (never a symlink), owned by a uid other than the guard's effective uid, and not group- or other-writable; a present sentinel failing any condition is IGNORED with the decision unchanged, recorded to guard-events and escape-spoof.json (a failed write is warned about in the hook's banner, or in the block reason of a denied stop, which has no banner; the warning asks for a manual record), and normally raised once by the next resume audit (again while its rename fails; a later sentinel recorded before that audit overwrites escape-spoof.json, leaving the earlier one only its guard-events row, where that append succeeded). Uid inequality proves not-self, never operator identity; on a shared-uid host no file either party can create passes, so the clean-ALLOW channel is unavailable there (recovery: a differently-owned sentinel such as a root-owned one, operator registry or mode maintenance, or the bounded marked exit; split-uid deployment is the recommended posture). The platform interrupt is a second, structurally unguardable escape, left uncovered on purpose. Blocker proofs are validated against their declared sources (the dispatch ledger, the pending-decisions surface, evidence freshness, the clock), but that whole substantiation surface (the backlog state/granted fields, a pending-decision row, the dispatch ledger, a not-before value, and free-text external evidence) is largely ACTOR-AUTHORABLE: the guard raises the bar (it rejects an unknown blocker kind and requires a substantiating record in the declared authoritative source) yet cannot categorically enforce that a block is granted by an authority other than the assistant, closed categorically only by operator-owned, assistant-non-writable records at the OS layer (SYSTEM-HARDENING.md entry 2). Plausibly FABRICATED external evidence in particular is not mechanically closable at this layer where no attestation register is declared; where one is declared, an external or foreign-lease blocker classifies blocked only when its ref is covered by a fresh validated attestation whose snapshot is re-anchored to the register authority and whose refs are re-derived from the register content at yield, so a swapped register or a fabricated-refs snapshot substantiates nothing; this raises the bar over free-text evidence but is not categorically forgery-proof, since the register is a separately-declared surface and filesystem write to it, wherever it is declared, forges an attestation by appending a valid approved row (uncommitted; the git or anchor authority checks only the committed or anchored prefix), closed categorically only by an operator-owned, assistant-non-writable register at the OS layer; the remaining residuals are cadence, since tamper misleads until the next audit or gate run, and relevance, since a resolving pointer can still be a misappropriated pretext that triage refutes). The human-decision class proves only that a pending-decision row exists, never that the item genuinely crosses the human-oversight threshold, which stays human judgement. Coverage is the rendered roster (Stop, TeammateIdle, the yield-tool matcher): a yield primitive outside that roster is uncovered, reconciled when the toolchain register changes. The dispatch ledger sees only hooked launch tools, so a task launched through an unhooked tool costs one spurious deny and a dead task read as live permits one idle until staleness catches it, both directions bounded and logged. An open or proposed id that vanishes from the enumeration without a closed receipt, OR (FIX 2) a previously-actionable id DEMOTED to proposed/ungranted without a closed receipt (the checkpoint records each id's eligibility for this), is injected as a cannot-evaluate by the anti-shrinkage checkpoint (backlog-checkpoint.json: the first window has no union to compare, and a drop forced by the checkpoint's id bound is logged to guard-events, a failed append warned about in the hook's output, so a drop is never silent; a checkpoint or init marker that cannot be written is named in the hook's output whether or not its guard-events row is written, and an unwritten checkpoint does not record that window's items, so one that then vanishes or is demoted before a later checkpoint write succeeds is not held as such unless an earlier checkpoint records it); that eligibility memory is itself in the actor-writable state dir, the same categorical residual. A bound-released ALLOW WITH FINDINGS past ANY non-closed disposition (actionable, cannot-evaluate, waiting, blocked, or proposed) is marked forced_unresolved (a guard-events row plus an append-only row in forced-exit.jsonl, each normally raised once, at least once if recording it in forced-exit-surfaced.json fails, a failed append of either surfacing in the warn banner itself) and is triaged by the next resume audit; no register row, attestation, or escape-adjacent artefact suppresses that record.

The TeammateIdle binding of the same decision core as orch-stop-guard, sharing its registry/lease scoping, escape, counter bound, and guard-events logging. A deny (exit 2) prevents the teammate from going idle past enumerated actionable work. On cannot-evaluate (an enumerator error or an unreadable proof source) it takes the STOP branch, which (FIX 1) now DENIES the idle (ignorance refuses the wind-down; a denied TeammateIdle cannot wedge the session, and the operator escape releases a genuine block); an unreadable registry or unresolvable cwd still fails OPEN at the binding. Same disclosed bounds as orch-stop-guard on ledger blind spots, fabricated blocker evidence and its attestation narrowing, escape-sentinel acceptance, the anti-shrinkage checkpoint, and the forced_unresolved marking of bound-released exits. Fires only where the platform emits TeammateIdle (doc-confirmed 2026-08-29); platforms without the event keep only the Stop and yield-tool bindings.

The scheduled-yield binding of the decision core: a call that parks the run (schedule_idle) or ends the loop (a ScheduleWakeup with stop=true is classified stop) is judged against a fresh enumeration. Registry-scoped and lease-scoped like orch-stop-guard; a tool the registry's yield_tools list does not name is out of scope even inside the matcher, and a registry yield tool OUTSIDE this fixed matcher is NOT covered (the doctor flags it; a manifest matcher is fixed at generation). On the schedule path a cannot-evaluate DENIES (missing evidence never licenses new autonomy; a denied tool call cannot wedge a session), bounded by a three-denial cap on an unchanged basis, after which it ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS so the guard cannot be farmed into bypass training. Each deny, the quiet-claim deny included, appends a guard-events row; a failed append leaves no row and adds a short recording-failure warning to the deny reason and the banner while the deny stands.
