gates.residue: Total over its declared surface, in three layers. Layer one, STATIC pre-launch: every check() call site in the registered runner's source is resolved to literal ids and that set must equal the hand-authored expectation manifest tools/selftest_checks.toml exactly before any child is launched; it resolves only direct bare-name check() call sites with string-literal or for-loop-literal ids (the loop attribution is the innermost enclosing for, lexical only: it does not model any intervening dataflow between the loop header and the call site, a rebinding of the loop variable or a nested function boundary, so such a site can mis-attribute its ids, caught, if at all, by the runtime set reconcile), and a non-call reference to the bare name check, a comprehension-bound id Name, any other unresolvable or duplicate source id, and source that does not parse are refused fail-closed, never silently resolved, while two static blind spots remain, bounded the same way: an invocation route the static layer never sees a call site for because it never names check as a bare Name in Load context (getattr, exec, an import that binds a different name and is then called through it, or a globals()['check'] lookup), and a rebinding of the name check the static layer cannot detect (any Store-class or non-Load binding: an assignment, a with-as or except-as target, a nested def check or class check, an import check, a del check, or a global or nonlocal declaration), which leaves the direct call sites visible and counted while they may no longer invoke the instrumented helper; both are caught, if at all, by the runtime set reconcile, a registered id whose only route is invisible (no direct call site at all) is refused by the static layer pre-launch as a registered id with no source check(), and the dead-direct-site decoy (a route that re-executes an already-registered id whose direct call site is dead) passes both set layers and is bounded only by the non-discrimination residual (a constant-true check counts as executed). Layer two, RUNTIME: the executed check-id set recorded at the instrumented check() choke point is emitted as a strict structured report and reconciled exactly against the same manifest, judged with the child's real exit code; missing, extra, or duplicate ids, a missing, malformed, wrong-suite, or non-regular report, a malformed manifest, and every cannot-evaluate fail closed, and a child exit 0 never overrides a missing or mismatched report. Layer three: the child carries its own in-run self-guard, reconciling the same set even on a direct developer run of an intact runner; the self-guard sits behind the runner's module entry, so it cannot fire once that entry is gone (the runner then exits 0 with no output and no report on a direct run, which this gate reports as cannot-evaluate only when it launches the runner itself), and the entry-guard gate holds that entry in place for every registered runner. The child suite's own behavioural assurance (the orchestrator-integrity acceptance vectors over hermetic fixtures, judged on structured verdicts) rides the child's verdict, which this gate requires; the gate launches that child under a git-neutral environment built in two layers (HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME pinned to a fresh empty directory, so the per-user global config, ignore, and attributes surfaces are empty for every descendant git call, including one made after a descendant scrubs the GIT_* environment and drops the GIT_* pins, plus, for the immediate child, ambient GIT_* dropped, the global and system config files pinned to os.devnull with GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, and core.excludesFile and core.attributesFile overridden to os.devnull by injected entries), and drops every ambient PYTHON*-prefixed variable from the child environment, transitively neutralizing PYTHONPATH/sitecustomize module injection into descendant interpreters (nothing downstream re-derives or re-sets a PYTHON* variable, and the runner's own interpreter grandchild launches carry -I -B as defence in depth for a direct developer run), which hardens the GATE-launched child only, the runner's own direct-invocation hermeticity being a separately tracked item; three launch-environment bounds are disclosed: the system-wide git config ($(prefix)/etc/gitconfig) is neutralized only for the immediate child (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and the GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pin are themselves GIT_-prefixed, so a scrubbing descendant drops them) and the system-wide attributes file ($(prefix)/etc/gitattributes) is not neutralized at all (no GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM is injected, and a scrubbing descendant would drop it the same way), a hostile system-wide file being root-owned, the same trust tier as the git binary itself and so at the threat-model boundary, outside what this gate defends, and git is resolved through the ambient PATH, a trusted-toolchain concern outside this gate's threat model, and the environment drop neutralizes the PYTHON*-prefixed family only, a loader-level injection control such as LD_PRELOAD and the interpreter binary itself sitting at the same trusted-toolchain tier, outside this gate's threat model. It proves SET IDENTITY AND EXECUTION only: it does not prove an invoked assertion is discriminating (a constant-true check counts as executed), carries no mutation sensitivity, sees nothing outside the instrumented check() helper (an assertion made by a direct FAILURES.append outside the choke point, whose non-execution is invisible to the execution set, a direct EXECUTED.append or _EXECUTED_SET.add that manufactures execution evidence for a check that never really ran, or a suite not registered), and cannot distinguish a legitimate from an illegitimate coordinated deletion of a check and its manifest row in one reviewed change. The static scan and the launch read the runner's source at two moments, so a concurrent same-user writer between them is outside this repo's sole-orchestrator threat model (the runtime layer still reconciles what actually ran); repo-root confirmation is a .git-existence proxy anchored to the gate's own file, not a full git-identity check; and the expectation manifest is trusted hand-authored input whose schema is machine-validated but whose completeness rests on source review. A row may carry an optional args list of literal arguments, forwarded to the runner ahead of the gate's own --execution-report pair; each must be a string of at most 200 characters from a closed printable-ASCII set (a letter or digit first, or one or two dashes and then one), and an argument that names, abbreviates, or attaches a value to --execution-report is refused, while any other shape is refused too. The filter is lexical: no row can redirect the report through the named option, and nothing more is claimed about what an accepted argument means to a given runner; a runner that writes no report (one that stops parsing, exits early, or takes the rest of its argv as data) is a missing report, cannot-evaluate, never a pass. Rows whose runners resolve to one path form a group: before any launch, every row of the requested suite's group must carry args no other row of the group carries, the rows' expected sets must be pairwise disjoint, and their union must equal the runner's static check() set exactly; a gap, an overlap, an extra id, or a missing or repeated args list is cannot-evaluate, and a single-row runner is held to the whole set exactly as before. Membership resolves every row's runner strictly, so a missing path, a non-directory component, a symlink loop or a permission error in any row's runner is cannot-evaluate before any report directory is allocated or any runner launched, never an assumed non-member, a runner path carrying a control or format character (C0, DEL, C1, the bidi controls, U+2028 and U+2029) is refused by the schema, and a suite id outside the closed suite-id grammar (a letter or digit first, then letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only) is refused by name, so a space-joined launch identity can never stand for a registered suite. Before any launch, every registered row must also have its launch line (check_selftest_execution.py --suite <id>) in both tools/run_all_checks.sh and .github/workflows/quality.yml, each read as a regular file through the parity gate's validated loader; a missing, non-regular, unreadable or loader-rejected roster, or a row whose launch line is missing from at least one of the two, is cannot-evaluate; a roster member counts as a launch line only when it is exactly check_selftest_execution.py --suite <id>, the one argv shape the gate's command line accepts, so a member carrying any further argument, or a near-miss id, launches nothing. That check is lexical: it proves each launch line is present, not that it runs or passes. The group rule is checked for the requested suite's group only, once per invocation, and launches that one row, so that every other row is launched rests on the lexical launch-line check; nor does the group rule prove that the runner's handling of its args selects the declared subset other than through the runtime reconcile of the row actually launched; a runner reached through a hard link or a byte copy under another path forms its own group, held alone to the whole static set, so an undetected group member can only be refused, never pass with a subset. Registered surface at this release: the orch-behaviour-selftest, ci-status-behaviour-selftest, git-fixture-env-core, git-fixture-env-config-combined, git-fixture-env-config-malformed, git-fixture-env-config-system, instruction-budget-selftest, python-floor-selftest, entry-guard-selftest, brief-capability-selftest, and hook-latency-selftest suites.

An adopter-parameterized scan that flags a hardcoded LITERAL value at an adopter-declared command sink (a command word plus an option name in a declared command-surface file), so a reusable command derives its target-specific parameter rather than baking one in (grdinp input-soundness, exetgt templated-target re-verification). It ships NO command, option, repository, or path of its own: with no .aiqt/derived-command-parameters.toml it is NOT APPLICABLE, and a present but unusable configuration fails closed. It covers a recognizable SUBSET (class c, partial): it proves only that the declared sink is NON-LITERAL (a reference to an allowed variable), never that the variable resolves at runtime to the correct target, which is exetgt's runtime confirmation outside any static scanner. Its lexical scanner does not model pipelines and grouping precisely, credits no command substitution as derived, matches a command by basename only (an alias, a function, a wrapper, or a dynamically constructed command word slips it), and reasons only over the option forms and reference-variable names the adopter declared, so an undeclared sink, an obfuscated or constructed literal, and a forge or tool the configuration does not name are outside it.

hooks.residue: A PATH guard, not a content judge: it decides where a write lands, never what it writes. Covers only PreToolUse Write, Edit, and MultiEdit calls carrying a readable file_path. TWO arming inputs, each fail-open on genuine ABSENCE only: the per-slice declaration write-scope.json, read at the orchestration registry-declared state_dir (resolved from the registry the guard reads EXACTLY ONCE, via the pure _state_dir_from_registry helper, never a second independently-faulting read; out of the slice tree by default but MAY be in-tree when the registry declares an in-tree state_dir), arms SLICE CONFINEMENT; the in-tree committed frozen floor .aiqt/frozen.json (generated by tools/gen_manifest.py from the ownership classification, drift-gated) arms the FROZEN layer. The structural other-repo/nested-repo denial applies to every covered write whose repository root resolves; the frozen-floor denial fires whenever a floor is PRESENT, and an armed session additionally requires one, so neither is unconditionally always-on and only an un-armed session with a genuinely-absent floor leaves the frozen layer inert. Slice confinement is fail-open on a missing declaration. The principled fail-open is genuine ABSENCE (of a declaration or floor: no confinement in effect, the same inert boundary gensrc and, by default, the orchestration suite use, whose truncation guard denies an absent registry in the opt-in registry-required mode); a cannot-evaluate FAULT is not absence and denies (see the fail posture below). The registry that LOCATES the declaration is part of the read: a bad or unreadable registry (an lstat fault, a read/parse error, a non-version-1 object, or a present-but-malformed state_dir) is a cannot-evaluate that DENIES rather than silently falling back to XDG and disarming confinement. Out-of-scope is a DENY, never an ASK (an ASK would hand the confined actor the click-through on its own confinement and would wedge an unattended run); the remedy is the harness re-declaring the slice, so scope-widening stays on the harness side, never a guarded-tool call. The declaration is machine-set inert data, never authored by the assistant through a guarded tool; the residual Bash-write path to the state dir remains, so the harness-set integrity is defence in depth, not categorical. Fail posture, by regime: a MISSING tool_name denies (the shared fail-closed contract); a malformed tool_name, an unreadable tool_input, a missing/empty file_path, or a control-character file_path denies as a malformed call in either regime; a covered write whose session repository root cannot be resolved (a missing/unreadable cwd or a non-git session) DENIES fail-closed in both regimes, because the root is resolved FIRST and containment cannot be evaluated without it, so this denial precedes any relative-path handling (a non-git relative-path write DENIES, it does not defer); only WHEN the root resolves does an un-armed relative file_path defer to the sibling absolute_paths hook (which owns the relative case, EN-8 making no cwd-trusting determination) and allow, while an armed relative file_path denies; an un-armed realpath/containment/nested-repo-probe FAULT now DENIES too (a cannot-evaluate: the guard cannot prove the target is in-repo and not nested, so it denies rather than allowing an unverified write), as the same fault does armed; a target proven OUTSIDE the session toplevel, or in a NESTED or FOREIGN git repository under or beside it (resolved via the scrubbed git toplevel of the target nearest existing ancestor, every ambient GIT_* removed so a decoy repo cannot redirect the read), denies in BOTH regimes UNLESS the target repo is an adopter-DECLARED COMPANION STORE (the sanctioned cross-repo path below); a present frozen floor with the target on it denies in both regimes (the floor outranks the allowlist, deny over allow), a present-but-malformed floor denies (cannot-evaluate), and an ABSENT floor is inert un-armed but denies while armed (an armed session must commit a floor, an explicit empty list being valid, so a Bash-deleted floor cannot silently downgrade an armed session); armed, a declaration that is unreadable, malformed, unknown-version, or whose worktree_root does not resolve to this repo (a stale, copied, or moved declaration) denies; an allow entry wholly on the frozen floor makes the declaration malformed and denies (a declaration cannot declare past the floor); a target in repo, not frozen, and in the declared slice scope allows silently, while one not in scope denies. Every deny appends a guard-events row (the over-fire metric) where the root is resolvable (with no resolvable root no row is attempted); a failed append leaves no row and adds a short recording-failure warning to the deny reason and the banner, never blocking or altering the denial. Matching is on canonicalized real paths with component-boundary tree containment (the gensrc idiom), never a raw string prefix; the declaration and floor share one entry grammar (a repo-root-relative POSIX path, a trailing / marks a tree, no absolute/backslash/./../control-char/wildcard component). The floor is enforced against the manifest CLASS set {derived, manifest-self, archive}. The RUNTIME value of that floor is un-lowerable by the constrained actor through the guarded tools (a guarded write to .aiqt/frozen.json is itself on the floor and denied); but its DEFINITION (FROZEN_CLASSES in tools/gen_manifest.py) is generator source that lands through pull-request review PLUS the drift gate, which detects an INCONSISTENT floor (a committed frozen.json that does not match a fresh regeneration), NOT an unauthorized-but-internally-consistent redefinition of the class set followed by regeneration; an independent floor-authorization mechanism is out of scope for this hook. The floor proves membership in its declared selector set only, not that the generation-time class mapping is semantically complete. Class c (partial), matching the sibling gensrc_guard: the control fires deterministically inside its Write|Edit|MultiEdit matcher, but the rules it enforces span write paths the matcher cannot see (Bash-mediated writes, NotebookEdit, filesystem MCP tools, any write outside the platform hook path), and its slice-arming state is machine-local, so CI cannot observe the confinement. The committed frozen floor .aiqt/frozen.json is a generated, drift-gated output backstopped at merge by the manifest-gen-drift gate (tools/gen_manifest.py --check), the gensrc-registry-drift gate (tools/gen_gensrc.py --check), and the independent manifest-integrity verifier (tools/check_manifest.py) (defence in depth, each catching the other residual; these CI gates are not removed or softened), but nothing backstops an uncommitted, out-of-scope-mutable, or cross-repository write through the uncovered channels. Realpath closes symlink escapes present at check time but not a post-check swap, hard-link alias, bind-mount change, or case-fold/Unicode alias between the lstat probe and the tool write (TOCTOU); an OS-level write sandbox is the stronger overlapping control where available. It is single-author by design: exactly one declaration, one writer, harness-replaced; it is confinement of the sole writer, not parallel-write collision arbitration. SANCTIONED COMPANION-STORE declaration (adopter-controlled config): the orchestration registry MAY declare companion_stores, a list of ABSOLUTE paths to git repo TOPLEVELS beside the session repo (for example the durable store the sole orchestrator owns, which is by design a SECOND git repo next to the code repo). A covered write whose target resolves - by EXACT repo-root match, the resolved git toplevel of the target EQUALLING a declared store root, never a prefix/substring - into a DECLARED companion store is ALLOWED and AUDITED (a guard-event row, kind wrtscp, decision allow, naming the declared store; where that append fails the write is still allowed, with a note saying the row could not be written) rather than denied, so the single most routine legitimate cross-repo write no longer inverts to deny-the-audited-path while the Bash residual stays open. The hook only HONOURS a validly-declared store, it never self-widens: per guard-input-soundness a declaration is honoured only if it is a non-empty absolute string resolving to a REAL git toplevel that IS the declared root itself; a MALFORMED, unresolvable, non-repo, or non-root declaration is fail-closed (silently dropped, the cross-repo write still DENIES), a bad entry can only remove a would-be allow and never open a hole, and the exact-root match means a write into a repo NESTED inside a declared store, or a sibling merely beside it, does NOT match. Declaring a store never defeats the frozen-floor or the nested-in-session denials. Declaring a companion store is a GUARDRAIL-CONFIGURATION change: companion_stores widens where covered writes may land (a cross-repo scope widening), so it is under the SAME human-authorization discipline as any other scope widening (guardrail-config-integrity) - the harness/adopter sets it, never the constrained actor. For that reason the orchestration LOCAL registry (.aiqt/orchestration.local.json) is on the hook-side ALWAYS-FROZEN set: a covered Write/Edit/MultiEdit to it is DENIED in BOTH regimes and INDEPENDENT of the committed frozen floor, so the actor cannot self-declare a companion_stores widening through a guarded tool (the general Bash-write path stays the disclosed residual). The companion_stores declaration is honoured only inside a VERSION-1 registry OBJECT: a registry with a missing or non-1 version reads as bad (a cannot-evaluate), so a declaration lacking "version": 1 yields NO stores and the cross-repo write FAILS CLOSED (denies), never silently taking effect. The declaration lives in the adopter/harness registry surface (exactly as state_dir does); this path guard reads it, it does not police who wrote the registry. DEADLINE: main() gives this check 8 seconds (the 10-second hook timeout less 2), counted from before its payload read, and fails closed with exit 2 when it has not decided by then; on the worst shapes the hooks self-test times, up to 1 MB, its slowest call took about 0.04 s in-process on a 24-core host with Python 3.14.4 (2026-10-15). Interpreter start-up and a wait the interpreter cannot interrupt (a read from a hung mount, a long call into C code) fall outside that deadline, and whether the platform blocks a call whose hook it stops at its own timeout is unverified. Where SIGALRM, setitimer or the main thread is unavailable, or SIGALRM is blocked, the check runs with no deadline; cleanup that runs while the deadline unwinds is outside it.

An ULTRA-CONSERVATIVE "recover-then-allow unless PRISTINE and provably clean" guard (EN-6; supersedes the GD-41 coarse cut and the EN-4 fail-open-lexical hook) with THREE outcomes: ALLOW (exit 0 silent), SNAPSHOT-THEN-ALLOW (an inert refs/aiqt-recovery/ snapshot is taken, then the discard is ALLOWED with a recovery note), and DENY (permissionDecision deny, blocks). NO-ASK posture: this guard never returns an ask; read every ASK below as that no-ask resolution, SNAPSHOT-THEN-ALLOW for a recoverable discard and DENY-and-educate when a warranted recovery snapshot cannot be made or the command cannot be classified or resolved. The recoverable SNAPSHOT-THEN-ALLOW is the characteristic behaviour; a confirmed whole-tree loss on a probed-dirty tree DENIES, BUT under a non-cosmetic ambient GIT_* var (an unresolvable repository view) even a whole-tree clobber is SNAPSHOT-THEN-ALLOWED with a best-effort cwd snapshot instead, because the guard cannot prove the target IS the session tree (only WITH a usable session cwd: with none, a destructive form under such an override DENIES, fail closed). It fails open (ALLOW) ONLY at the true boundary - a command with no git command-word, no recognized lossy verb, or an unparseable command (a tokenizer ValueError) that names no lossy verb keyword - because that is not a discard it can reason about. WITHIN scope (a recognized lossy verb: checkout/switch/restore/reset/clean/stash/rm/branch) the outcome is ASK UNLESS the command is a PRISTINE SINGLE BARE `git <verb>` invocation AND (for a lossy form) the whole working tree is PROVABLY CLEAN, or the form is genuinely non-destructive, in which cases ALLOW. PRISTINE SINGLE BARE is judged PURELY LEXICALLY (the bash grammar is NEVER parsed): after optional leading KEY=value assignments the command is exactly `git <args>` as ONE simple command, and the RAW string carries NO shell metacharacter ANYWHERE, EVEN INSIDE QUOTES - none of `;` `|` `&` `<` `>` `(` `)` `{` `}` `$` backtick backslash `!` newline, which by construction also rules out `&&`/`||`/`|&`, EVERY redirection form (`>`, `>>`, `<`, `2>`, `&>`, `>&`, `n>&m`, a leading or interspersed redirect), and EVERY command/process substitution (backtick, `$( )`, `<( )`, `>( )`) - AND no shell reserved word (if/then/elif/else/fi/for/while/until/do/done/case/esac/function/select/`[[`/`]]`/`{`/`}`) AND a command word that is LITERALLY `git` (not a path like /usr/bin/git, and not a wrapper: command/exec/builtin/env/xargs/time/`!`/sudo/nice/timeout/nohup/sh -c/bash -c). ANY shell metacharacter, wrapper, redirect, reserved word, second command, or option the classifier cannot resolve makes the command not-pristine, and it ASKS WITHOUT consulting the probe (a deliberate safe over-ask): treating the mere presence of shell structure in a lossy-verb command as an ASK is how the guard avoids modelling shell semantics it cannot model soundly. Only a metacharacter-free `git <verb> <plain args>` reaches the probe. PROVABLY CLEAN means the ONE read-only probe - `git -c status.showUntrackedFiles=all status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` (config-forced so a repo-local status.showUntrackedFiles=no CANNOT hide an untracked file, 5s timeout, offline) - reports NO tracked change (staged or unstaged, either column) AND NO untracked (`??`) entry; an untracked file is uncommitted work a force-checkout/clean/reset can destroy, so it counts as DIRTY (only an ignored `!!` entry is treated as clean). When a pristine bare lossy form is on a provably-clean tree it ALLOWs (nothing the probe can see to lose); a pristine bare WHOLE-TREE-clobbering verb (reset --hard by effective last-wins mode, checkout -f with no pathspec, switch --force/--discard-changes) on a probed-DIRTY tree DENIES (the reason wording covers untracked-only-dirty too); everything else in scope ASKS. There is NO claim that any compound, wrapped, redirected, or non-pristine form the guard RECOGNIZES as in-scope is proven safe: those are never ALLOWED, only ASKED (no in-band override exists); the one exception is a command word `git` or a verb built in a way no raw, joined or de-quoted reading of the text assembles (a disclosed residual below), which reads as out-of-scope and is silently ALLOWED, not ASKED. A dirty tree ALONE does not force that outcome on a PRISTINE bare form: a dirty-tree WHOLE-TREE clobber DENIES and other non-pristine or redirected forms ASK, but a genuinely non-destructive form (reset --soft, plain switch, checkout -b, clean -n) can still ALLOW on a dirty tree when no redirect or ambient override applies. Verb forms (each ALLOWs only as a pristine bare command on a provably-clean tree, except the unconditional-allow and unconditional-ask forms noted): checkout - a plain unforced branch-create (-b/--orphan) with NO merge option is an unconditional allow (git carries changes and aborts on conflict), and the NEW-BRANCH NAME argument of -b/-B (attached -bfoo or separated -b foo) is parsed as that name, never char-scanned as clustered force flags, so -bfoo/-bBranch ALLOW and are never mis-read as carrying -f/-B (F-85); -B is a force branch-create/RESET that overwrites an existing branch ref and can orphan committed commits, so it ASKS (including when combined with other flags); a -m/--merge or --conflict[=<style>] merge-switch, WITH or WITHOUT a -b create, does a three-way merge that can overwrite local changes and is worktree-scoped, decided before the branch-create allow (F-88); -p/--patch, any pathspec/bare-operand form, or a forced -f -b branch-create is worktree-scoped; -f with no pathspec is a whole-tree clobber. switch - -f/--force/--discard-changes is a clobber; -C/--force-create is a force branch-create/RESET that overwrites an existing branch ref and can orphan committed commits, so it ASKS; --merge/-m and --conflict[=<style>] are worktree-scoped (a three-way merge can overwrite local changes); a plain switch or an unforced -c create with NO merge option preserves non-conflicting local changes and aborts rather than lose them, so it is an unconditional allow, and the NEW-BRANCH NAME argument of -c/-C (attached -cfoo or separated -c foo) is parsed as that name, never char-scanned as clustered force flags, so -cfeature ALLOWs and is never mis-read as carrying -f/-C (F-85). restore - EVERY form is worktree-scoped, including --staged (it can erase staged-only content). reset - effective --hard clobbers; --soft is an unconditional allow (HEAD-only, index and worktree intact); --merge/--mixed/--keep/path-scoped/no-mode are scoped (index-changing); an ambiguous bare --m is scoped. rm - EVERY form is worktree-scoped, including --cached. clean - ANY non-dry-run clean is an unconditional ASK (untracked files are a different, unrecoverable asset, and the guard does not model whether the clean would fire, closing the clean.requireForce/-q/-i/clustered-flag edges); a -n/--dry-run judged before any `--` allows, BUT when an arg-consuming option -e/--exclude is present the `-n` is not trusted (it may be the exclude pattern) so the clean routes to its ASK. Destructive options are matched by CONSERVATIVE PREFIX (--patc=--patch, --del=--delete, --dis=--discard-changes, --har=--hard, --mer=--merge are unambiguous abbreviations git accepts; an AMBIGUOUS force-prefix like --for, which git itself REJECTS for branch as ambiguous with --format and for switch as ambiguous with --force-create, is treated as force ANYWAY, erring safe rather than recognizing only spellings git would accept); a `--`/`--end-of-options` boundary is respected so an operand after it (git clean -f -- -nasty, git rm -f -- --cached) is a pathspec, never a safe-looking option. stash drop/clear ASK, and stash export ASK for every spelling (F-95: export writes stash state to a ref, and --to-ref overwrites an arbitrary ref unconditionally); branch force forms ASK - -D/--delete --force (force delete), -M/--move --force (force rename), -C/--copy --force (force copy), -f/--force with an operand (force reset), and a delete (-d/-D/--delete) combined with -r/--remotes (F-94: deleting remote-tracking refs, which git force-removes past the merged-branch safeguard) - while a plain create/list, a local non-remotes -d, and an unforced -m/-c stay allow, and an attached -u<upstream> value (-ufoo, -u <upstream>) is parsed as the upstream, never scanned as a clustered force flag. A `git -C <dir> ...` or a GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE-prefixed form is pristine-lexically but names a worktree the guard cannot resolve to the session cwd, so it ASKS rather than trust a session-dir probe. An AMBIENT GIT_*-prefixed var in the process env also forces ASK unless it is one of a small COSMETIC allowlist (UI/editor/pager/prompt/lock/identity vars that cannot change the discard target, the object/ref view, the index, or dirtiness detection): the probe scrubs every ambient GIT_* and reads the real cwd repo, but the guard cannot scrub them from the ACTUAL command, which still inherits them and may act on a different git dir, work tree, index, or object/ref view, so the guard cannot prove the repository view the ACTUAL command uses IS the session cwd. Under any such non-cosmetic ambient var EVERY in-scope pristine form ASKS - a destructive clobber AND an otherwise-non-destructive allow form (reset --soft, plain switch, clean -n, checkout -b) alike, checked BEFORE the role/allow logic - each DESTRUCTIVE form with a best-effort cwd snapshot WHEN the session cwd is a not-provably-clean snappable tree (a provably-clean cwd takes none, a NON-DESTRUCTIVE allow form takes none, and a stash/branch-only form takes none; NO usable session cwd DENIES a destructive form, fail closed, and takes none; the snapshot may not capture a redirected tree), so no allow form and no clean cwd probe wins a silent ALLOW under such a redirect. A GIT_TRACE* var is NOT cosmetic: an absolute GIT_TRACE value makes the ACTUAL command append trace output to that path (which could be a repo file), so it too forces ASK (the recovery/probe git calls still scrub the whole GIT_TRACE family, so THEY write no trace, but the ambient GIT_TRACE on the command itself is not neutralized). This is FAIL-SAFE by construction rather than a fixed enumeration (which kept missing new members - GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE, GIT_REFERENCE_BACKEND - and more will exist): an unknown or new non-cosmetic GIT_* var ASKS rather than winning a silent ALLOW. This control is SIDE-EFFECTING (EN-6 recovery layer): before it ALLOWS or ASKS a snapshottable in-scope discard (checkout/switch/restore/reset/rm/clean) whose worktree it can resolve to the session cwd AND whose tree is NOT provably clean, it takes an INERT recovery snapshot of the uncommitted work and appends one line to an EXTERNAL per-user ledger, so a discard that is asked-then-approved OR wrongly allowed by a mis-parse is still recoverable (the hook fires once, with no post-approval callback). An ACCEPTED non-pristine in-scope command (one the closed allowlist grammar below admits) is snapshot-backed against EACH worktree the grammar resolves - the literal -C chain of a plain git segment over the &&-followed literal cd chain - PLUS the SESSION CWD repo as a best-effort catch-all for EVERY in-scope command (a verb that actually acts on the session repository stays recoverable even when no segment resolved it); a resolved plain stash drop/clear first preserves the stash of its target repository under durable refs or DENIES (worktree cleanliness never establishes stash safety); a discard-capable segment whose directory the grammar cannot establish DENIES (fail closed); on snapshot fail the decision stays ASK; and with NO session cwd EVERY non-pristine in-scope command DENIES (fail closed: no catch-all snapshot base resolves) - a DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE cost that also denies otherwise-legitimate no-cwd forms whose visible shape is non-destructive or non-snapshottable, such as a compound checkout -b, a piped git log, or an assignment-prefixed clean -n or reset --soft, each of which allows in its bare or with-cwd form. The snapshot uses a TEMPORARY GIT_INDEX_FILE outside the repo (seeded by copying the real index), `git add --all` (captures tracked-modified + UNTRACKED; ignored excluded), `git write-tree`, `git commit-tree` (parent = HEAD when present), and a CREATE-ONLY `git update-ref refs/aiqt-recovery/<utc-ts>-<pid> <sha>` with an empty expected-old value (a name collision FAILS the snapshot rather than clobbering a prior recovery ref). The snapshot writes only git objects and one private ref (plus a reflog entry for it when core.logAllRefUpdates=always, or when a reflog already exists for the ref) and does NOT itself touch the real index, worktree, HEAD, or any branch; the ref is invisible to plain `git status`, `git branch`, and `git log` but is reachable via `git log --all` / `git for-each-ref refs/aiqt-recovery` / `git show-ref` (a real ref, not hidden). Every real-state git call in this control takes an ALLOWLIST posture, scrubbing EVERY ambient GIT_*-prefixed var rather than enumerating a family (successive reviews kept finding new members: GIT_CONFIG_*, then GIT_TRACE*, then GIT_ATTR_SOURCE), so an ambient decoy repo (GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE), an ambient `git -c` (GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS) config injection, an ambient GIT_ATTR_SOURCE attribute-source redirect, or an ambient GIT_TRACE that would make a read-only call WRITE a trace file cannot reach these calls; the scrub itself re-asserts GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (so the scrub cannot strip the offline + non-interactive posture: no partial-clone lazy-fetch over the network, no prompting) plus a FIXED INTERNAL recovery identity (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=aiqt-recovery, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=aiqt-recovery@localhost) so the snapshot `git commit-tree` never depends on an ambient or on-disk user.name/user.email the scrub removed - which would make it FAIL where no git identity is configured (a CI runner or fresh install with no global gitconfig), silently disabling the recovery backstop - and a recovery commit is deterministically attributed to the guard, not the user, the callers re-apply only the few vars they set themselves AFTER the scrub (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS for the read-only probe, a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE for a snapshot), and any GIT_* the call genuinely needed but was scrubbed fails SAFE to a probe/snapshot failure (fail-to-ASK, never a silent allow). This closes the whole ambient-env class at once; the residual is NOT limited to on-disk config - it spans the non-GIT_ environment (HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/PATH/TMPDIR), on-disk git configuration AND attributes (repo/global/system .gitconfig and .gitattributes), index and ignore state, submodules and embedded repos, configured hooks and filters, PATH-based git resolution, and partial-clone object availability, all read by git by design. RESIDUAL (the honest bound on "inert"): the inert property is BOUNDED, not categorical, because git may ADDITIONALLY run a git-configured (repo, global, system, or command-scope) program during the snapshot whose effect is outside this guard control - a clean/process filter runs on `git add --all` (the CHECK-IN / clean direction, NOT smudge, which would run only on a restore/checkout), an fsmonitor hook runs on the `git status` probe, and a reference-transaction hook plus a post-index-change hook can run on the temp-index write and on the `git update-ref`; a clean filter can TRANSFORM the captured bytes, so the snapshot is NOT guaranteed byte-exact on a filtered repo; and a single overlaid tree cannot capture dirty content inside a SUBMODULE or an untracked EMBEDDED git repo (it stores only the gitlink) and flattens staged-vs-unstaged into ONE tree. The ledger is `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/aiqt-guardrails/recovery.jsonl` (normally outside the repo, so a `git clean` cannot destroy it). The ledger write is BEST-EFFORT: normally one line per snapshot, but skipped when no per-user location resolves (absent HOME/XDG), when that path would resolve inside the repo, or when the directory or write fails. A written line records: utc ts, repo path, the triggering git VERB (never the raw command or file contents), the recovery ref, the snapshot sha, the covered classes (tracked/staged/untracked), and the exact restore command (`git checkout <ref> -- :/`, OVERLAY mode: it brings back modified and new content but does NOT re-apply a recorded file deletion; for an exact, deletion-inclusive restore use an isolated branch via `git switch -c aiqt-recover-<id> <ref>`). The snapshot is decision-INDEPENDENT (it does not trust the form-classifier), so it also fires on a genuinely-safe snapshottable form (reset --soft, plain switch, checkout -b, clean -n) on a dirty tree, an accepted over-snapshot; it is SKIPPED on a provably-clean tree, out of scope, and for stash/branch (a worktree snapshot cannot capture stash entries or branch commits). FAIL POSTURE: when a warranted snapshot cannot be made (probe/write error, an undecodable non-UTF-8 path, over a ~100 MiB changed-content size cap, a bare or broken git dir, or a temp dir resolving inside the repo) it NEVER becomes a silent allow of a not-provably-clean discard - a would-be ALLOW is DOWNGRADED to ASK ("no recovery point could be created"), and an already-ASK/DENY decision is left as-is with the failure surfaced. Retention is NOT handled here (refs accumulate; auto-pruning is a separate maintenance op, never inside PreToolUse). NO IN-BAND OVERRIDE: the former `GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=1` command prefix is REMOVED. The guarded assistant could type it into the very command under guard, so it could not carry the operator-only authority it claimed, and it skipped the recovery snapshot. A leading GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD assignment (`=` or `+=`, any value) is now an ordinary env assignment, and no code path reads its value to permit anything. Two code paths read the name, and only these two: `_segment_dir_simple` counts it as a benign assignment that redirects nothing (any other leading assignment, such as `FOO=1`, counts as a possible redirect), and the migration sentence below, which adds reason text only. BOUNDED EQUIVALENCE: when the same command without the prefix already names a recognized work-losing git verb, and the prefixed command is a pristine single bare git command (the shell lexer parses it and its raw string carries no shell metacharacter), the prefixed command gets the decision and the snapshot of the command without it, because past the pristine gate the guard decides from the token list plus the raw-scan lossy-keyword flag, which the command without the prefix already set. When the command without the prefix names no such verb, it is allowed silently at the true boundary, and a pristine prefixed command can get nothing more permissive than that. Outside that bound the value is ordinary text in the raw command string, which the conservative raw scans of the guard read like any other text, so the decision can differ from the one the command gets without the prefix: (a) a value carrying a shell metacharacter, even quoted (`GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=";" git reset --hard`), makes the command not pristine; (b) a value that leaves a quote unbalanced (`GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD="1 git reset --hard`, which bash itself rejects) makes the command unparseable; (c) on an unparseable command every raw-flagged form is denied by the unparseable-command fallback, so the prefixed, the FOO-prefixed and the unprefixed spellings of an unparseable `git reset --hard <<EOF` whose heredoc body holds a lone quote all DENY alike; (d) the scope scan reads a git or work-losing-verb keyword inside the value, so `GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=reset git log -1` is in scope and DENIES as a flagged subcommand outside the recognized set, where `git log -1` is allowed. In case (a) on a dirty session tree the command gets a best-effort snapshot then ALLOW-with-note (DENY if the snapshot fails) where the bare whole-tree clobber DENIES, and with no session cwd a DENY (fail closed: the session-directory snapshot base cannot be resolved, exactly as for `FOO=<the same value>`); in case (b) it gets the unparseable-command fallback, where every raw-flagged unparseable command DENIES, exactly as the bare unparseable form does. No code on the non-pristine path or the unparseable-command fallback reads the name, so there the prefixed command gets exactly what the same command with `FOO=<the same value>` gets. These are existing behaviours of the raw scans and the non-pristine path that any leading assignment, metacharacter or second command reaches, not a property of this prefix. For this release only, a truthy one on a pristine bare command also adds a reason sentence stating that the override was removed and that `git stash` then the discard is the route (an unparseable or non-pristine command gets no such sentence); the next release deletes that sentence, the helper that adds it and its self-test vectors. For an intentional discard on a dirty tree, `git stash` (with `-u` for untracked files) then the discard reaches the provably-clean ALLOW with the work recoverable in the stash. The prefix no longer skips a recovery snapshot: no code path reads its value to skip one, so within the bounded equivalence above a prefixed command takes the snapshot the command takes without it, and on the non-pristine path and the unparseable-command fallback the snapshot `FOO=<the same value>` takes (the forms that take none, such as a ref-level or stash/branch asset and an ignored file, take none with or without it; the no-session-cwd non-pristine path above DENIES and takes none). The operator channel for a standing exemption is the hook configuration (disable or reconfigure the hook). HONEST RESIDUAL: being a LEXICAL hook it does NOT catch a git alias (config-defined; an inline `-c alias.<name>=...` now ASKS) or shell function that renames git or expands to a work-losing verb, a discard performed OUTSIDE the Bash tool, or persistent shell/config state set in a PRIOR turn. It also does NOT catch a real discard whose VERB is OUTSIDE the recognized set AND unflagged by the raw scan: a `git worktree remove -f` (or `--force`) of a dirty linked worktree discards the uncommitted work in that worktree, but `worktree` matches no lossy keyword, so the command is allowed at the true boundary; that verb is deliberately NOT added this round (disclosure matches the best-effort posture). By contrast (F-97), a command the raw scan DOES flag as in-scope whose resolved subcommand is nonetheless outside the recognized set (`git checkout-index -a -f`, `git read-tree -u --reset HEAD`, flagged by their `checkout`/`reset` substring) is NO LONGER silently allowed - it ASKS, since a flagged sub the classifier cannot resolve to a known verb cannot be proven non-destructive, and its sub is not snapshottable so no recovery point exists. It also does NOT catch obfuscation of the COMMAND WORD `git` ITSELF or of the verb that no reading of the text assembles. The scope scan reads the raw text, the text with its line continuations joined, and a copy with quotes, a $ before a quote, and backslashes removed, all unstripped, on a certain and an uncertain reading alike, so a wrapped reset fragmented by quotes or a backslash (env git followed by a quote-broken re-set, alone or after another git command) or a command word quote-broken so it spells git only after the shell strips the quotes (under a wrapper such as command or env) is in scope, where the closed allowlist grammar below DENIES it (no wrapper is an accepted command word). A word built another way (an escape decoded inside an ANSI-C quote, or a parameter expansion or command substitution evaluated at run time) reads as "no recognized lossy verb" and is silently ALLOWED, so the claim that any wrapper ASKS is NOT categorical: it holds only while one of those readings sees a contiguous git+verb keyword. This is a disclosed best-effort residual (the guard targets the accidental case, not an adversary deliberately building the command word or the verb at run time). When the shell reading is uncertain (any unquoted #, <<, ( or ), a lone { or } word, any backtick or $(, a line continuation the lexer reads differently once joined, or a form the lexer refuses), the same readings decide the scope, so a quote-fragmented verb in such a command is in scope. The joined reading brings a verb that a continuation splits under a wrapper into scope, and the de-quoted copy makes a quote-broken subcommand outside the recognized set (a fragmented checkout-index) deny like its plain spelling; a command the lexer refuses is flagged from its de-quoted copy too and then denies like every flagged unparseable command, so a split or quote-fragmented -C, --git-dir, --work-tree or cd redirect never reaches a session-directory snapshot. The probe ITSELF can be made to under-report dirtiness by git config or index state: an `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` mark on a tracked file, or a `submodule.<name>.ignore` setting, hides real modifications from `git status`, so the guard can read a genuinely-dirty tree as provably clean and ALLOW a discard of that hidden work; and the recovery snapshot ALSO cannot capture assume-unchanged/skip-worktree content (it is not in what `git add --all` re-stages) nor IGNORED files (git add --all excludes them; an ignored file overwritten by a forced checkout or removed by `clean -x` is unprobed - to avoid asking on every repo carrying build artifacts - and unsnapshotted). Beyond that, being ultra-conservative it OVER-FIRES heavily - every compound or metacharacter-bearing command that names a lossy verb is at best snapshot-then-allowed and at worst denied even when it would have been safe (no in-band override exists); a command that pipes or wraps a plain git segment (`git log | grep branch`) and a NON-GIT segment that contains a git word as TEXT (`echo git branch`) each DENY under the positive grammar when a lossy keyword puts the command in scope, because the raw scan matches the keywords wherever they appear and the grammar refuses every byte and command word outside its closed lists (a safe-direction over-deny, not narrowed: narrowing the raw scan is the whack-a-mole GD-34 rejected); the copy with quotes, a $ before a quote, and backslashes removed is matched the same way, so quoted prose whose words spell git and a lossy verb only once the quotes are removed (an echo or printf of a quote-broken git re-set, such as `echo "git re""set --hard"`) is in scope although the shell runs only echo or printf, and the grammar DENIES that harmless command (echo, printf and a double quote are outside it), while a read-only git subcommand whose quoted argument spells a lossy keyword only once the quotes are removed (`git log --grep="re""set"`) DENIES as an unrecognized flagged subcommand, as its plain spelling already did (kept, not narrowed: quoted text is code under eval, bash -c or sh -c, and this reading is what brings a fragmented verb there into scope); and a pristine whole-tree clobber over-DENIES on a dirty tree even when the specific target would have lost nothing - an accepted, recoverable cost of never silently allowing a real WORKING-TREE-CONTENT discard for a recognized command that is NOT covered by a disclosed residual. That no-silent-allow property is bounded to working-tree content: ref-level moves (reset --soft moving HEAD, a merged-branch delete) are reflog-recoverable, and the obfuscation/config residuals above are best-effort, not categorical. PR #423 replaces the earlier modelling walk with a POSITIVE LITERAL closed allowlist grammar, judged directly on the RAW string of every non-pristine in-scope command, so shell behaviour is never modelled on this path: anything the grammar does not spell out is denied by construction. THE GRAMMAR, exactly: every token is a bare literal word over the character class of letters, digits and _ . / @ : = + , % -, or ONE single-quoted literal containing no quote, standing alone as a whole token; the accepted command words, spelled bare and unquoted, are git, cd (option flags -P and -L only, exactly one operand, an absolute literal path with no parent-directory component whose realpath equals its normpath, so no symlink component), and true or : with no arguments; no assignment word (NAME=value) is accepted in or before a command-word position, and a GIT_* assignment-shaped token ANYWHERE in the command denies; a git segment accepts no global option but -C with an absolute literal path under the same rules, and its bare subcommand must be on the explicit read-only allowlist (status, log, rev-parse, rev-list, ls-files, ls-tree, cat-file, grep, describe, shortlog, name-rev, merge-base, check-ignore, check-attr, count-objects, show-ref, for-each-ref, var, version; ls-remote is DELISTED, because its --upload-pack/-u option runs an arbitrary command string and the subcommand itself opens network access, and help, diff, show and blame are DELISTED, because their ACCEPTED command line can run a configured program through git itself: git help launches a man viewer or browser and a configured man.<tool>.cmd is shell-evaluated, while the patch output of diff, show and blame runs configured textconv and external-diff drivers; -p/--patch is outside every closed option allowlist for the same reason - removed from every read-only option list AND denied on the modelled lossy verbs checkout, restore, reset and stash (the push and save forms included; a digit-led cluster such as -2p and a flag hidden behind a consumed separated option value included, every declared option value consumed by its arity first), on the pristine single-command path and the grammar path alike, because interactive patch mode renders its hunks through the configured interactive.diffFilter program - and for-each-ref --format AND --sort are delisted because the %(...) placeholders and the sort atoms include signature fields that run the configured signature program) AND, for a read-only subcommand, carry ONLY the VETTED option spellings of that subcommand (exact value-less flags plus value-taking options accepted ONLY in the joined --opt=value spelling git itself reads joined - NEVER a separated value word, which git reads as a token in its own right: an earlier revision consumed a following word as an optional value, so git log --pretty --output=<path> passed vetting while git read --output as an option of its own and truncated the path - with no abbreviation even where git accepts an unambiguous prefix, each option value shape-validated, the log --pretty/--format value restricted to EXACTLY the seven named formats oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference and raw or to a string carrying the format: or tformat: prefix over an explicit placeholder allowlist that excludes every %G signature placeholder (EVERY other value denies, abbreviations and further built-in names such as email included, because git resolves an unprefixed value as a built-in format name or a pretty.<name> CONFIGURATION alias, and a configured alias can itself carry %G), a -- token ending the option region with every later token a positional operand, and a non-option token passed through as a positional operand - a rev, path, pattern or object name: DATA to the subcommand that receives it, never inert), because a read-only SUBCOMMAND is not a read-only COMMAND LINE: an unvetted option can run a program (git grep --open-files-in-pager/-O runs one per matching file) or write a file (git log --output=<path> truncates that file), so any option outside the vetted set denies naming itself; an explicit git stash list carries NO argument and an explicit git stash show carries AT MOST ONE positional stash reference and nothing else, no option-shaped token and no "--" (git forwards stash list arguments to git log and stash show arguments to git diff, where they would ride around the vetted grammar and the delisted diff class, and a retained "--" makes git stash show itself select patch output), a rule applied on the pristine single-command path and the grammar path alike; or a modelled lossy verb, which is then preserve-then-allowed exactly as the pin does (a resolved stash drop/clear preserves the stash of that repository under durable refs first or denies; a resolved worktree discard is snapshotted at its resolved target or denies; and the session cwd is ALWAYS snapshotted as the catch-all for every in-scope command), carrying ONLY the CLOSED option allowlist of that verb - exact spellings with each value-taking option consuming its value by arity; any other option denies naming itself, and git branch lists no --sort, --format, --edit-description or --list spelling, because the sort atoms and format placeholders include signature fields that run the configured signature program and --edit-description launches the editor (the ACCEPTED -m/--merge and --conflict spellings and the accepted stash pop and apply forms DO run the git-internal content merge, which honours a configured merge.<driver>.driver program on paths whose attributes select that driver - a DISCLOSED residual among the configured programs, bounded like the clean-filter and hook classes above, not a claim that an accepted lossy form runs no configured program) - while a compound that CONSUMES a stash entry (git stash pop, git stash branch) together with another lossy verb denies outright, because a successful pop applies then drops the entry, so the following verb can destroy the just-applied content while the dropped entry is gone and the pre-command snapshot cannot contain it (a bare consuming command alone keeps its handling); a git stash resolves its operation ONLY from its FIRST argument: a bare first word is the explicit operation, while no argument, a leading option of any spelling (-q, -m <msg>, an attached -m<msg>, --message=<msg>) or a leading -- token reads as a bare or implicit push (safe) - git itself refuses an implicit push carrying a stray bare token, and never runs one as a drop or clear - so a message value or a pathspec named drop or clear is never read as the operation; the joins are the && operator, the semicolon and the newline only, with a trailing semicolon and leading or trailing newlines accepted (bash runs the same commands) while a trailing && and any doubled or misplaced operator denies, and a cd is honoured for a later segment only across && joins (across a semicolon or newline the cd may have failed with the next command still running, so the directory becomes unprovable and a later discard-capable segment denies); the redirections accepted are >/dev/null, 2>/dev/null and 2>&1 only, none of which writes a file; an accepted redirect may directly follow a completed bare or quoted word (the word ends at the operator, exactly as bash reads it), an all-digit word standing immediately before the > operator is an IO number of which only 2 is accepted, and repeated accepted redirects are accepted. ANYTHING ELSE DENIES, naming the violation class: every other byte (a dollar sign, a backquote, a double quote, a backslash, a glob or brace character, a tilde, a comment hash, any <, which rules out every heredoc, here-string, process substitution and input or read-write redirect, a parenthesis, a pipe, a stray ampersand, a control byte), every quoting form beyond one standalone single-quoted literal, every other command word (echo, printf, test, [, pwd, pushd, popd, export, eval, source, ., set, unset, alias, every wrapper and interpreter, every quoted, concatenated or pathed spelling), every assignment word, every other git global option (-c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --no-pager and the rest), every unlisted subcommand (git commit or git push inside an in-scope compound included, and the delisted ls-remote), every unvetted or abbreviated read-only option (the deny names the offending spelling), every unresolvable or symlinked cd or -C path, every other join or redirect, and a trailing && (a trailing semicolon or newline is accepted, as stated above). THE FALLBACK COST, disclosed: an UNPARSEABLE command (a tokenizer ValueError) whose FULL raw text or its de-quoted copy the scan flags - git plus a work-losing verb keyword; heredoc bodies are NO LONGER stripped anywhere on this guard, because stripping removes text and so can only hide a real discard - is DENIED outright, read-only and prose-only forms included, with NO session snapshot and NO stash preservation; only an unparseable command the scan clears on both readings is allowed at the true boundary. The same no-stripping rule brings a PARSEABLE command whose quoted-heredoc prose merely mentions a lossy keyword in scope, where the grammar denies the heredoc operator itself: a disclosed over-deny in the safe direction. WHAT THE GRAMMAR DOES NOT COVER, disclosed: it proves nothing about a command it accepts beyond the shapes above - the vetted read-only option lists are a point-in-time audit of the named spellings against the program-running and file-writing options git documents (a future or renamed git option outside the vetted set denies rather than runs, an over-deny by design); REPOSITORY, GLOBAL OR SYSTEM CONFIGURATION CAN MAKE EVEN AN ACCEPTED READ-ONLY GIT COMMAND RUN A CONFIGURED PROGRAM - core.fsmonitor runs its monitor on git status, textconv and external-diff drivers run where file content or patches are rendered, a configured pager or viewer can run on any command that pages, a configured signature program runs where signatures are read, and configured clean/smudge/process FILTER DRIVERS (filter.<driver>.clean, .smudge and the long-running .process) run where git checks content in or out - so the grammar bounds the COMMAND LINE, never configuration, and a positional operand is DATA passed to the read-only subcommand that receives it, not inert; an accepted literal path is checked lexically and by realpath only (a mount, bind mount or rename race can still make the directory git uses diverge); acceptance of true and : assumes the shell builtins, which a function defined in a PRIOR turn outside this command could shadow; and the raw-scan scope residual of the pin is unchanged (a real discard whose verb is outside the recognized set AND unflagged, such as git worktree remove -f, is still allowed at the true boundary, and a git or verb spelling fragmented in a way no raw, joined or de-quoted reading assembles reads as out of scope). DEFERRED, tracked as later work: accepting a vetted wrapper form (env/nice/timeout with an inert prefix), a vetted interpreter form (sh -c or bash -c with a single literal body), and a vetted xargs form; each now denies with a re-issue-plainly education. Newly denied legitimate spellings, each with its plain allowed alternative: echo or printf beside a discard in one command denies, run the discard alone or join plain git, cd, true and : segments with &&; a relative or symlinked cd or -C path denies, use a literal absolute physical path; a cosmetic GIT_* assignment or a colour/pager -c key on a non-pristine discard denies, drop the assignment or option (the pristine single-command spelling keeps them); a heredoc in an in-scope command denies, feed data from a file instead; an expansion, substitution or double-quoted token denies, spell the operand as a bare or single-quoted literal. The plain read-only and modelled forms (git stash list, show and apply, git status, git log, an &&-joined literal absolute cd before a plain discard, and a literal git -C <abs> discard, each preserve-then-allowed) still allow. DEADLINE: main() gives this check 8 seconds (the 10-second hook timeout less 2), counted from before its payload read, and fails closed with exit 2 when it has not decided by then; on the worst shapes the hooks self-test times, up to 1 MB, its slowest call took 1.77 to 2.17 s in-process on a 24-core host with Python 3.14.4 that was running other work (runs on 2026-10-17; which clock those runs read, CPU or wall-clock time, was not recorded). Interpreter start-up and a wait the interpreter cannot interrupt (a read from a hung mount, a long call into C code) fall outside that deadline, and whether the platform blocks a call whose hook it stops at its own timeout is unverified. Where SIGALRM, setitimer or the main thread is unavailable, or SIGALRM is blocked, the check runs with no deadline; cleanup that runs while the deadline unwinds is outside it.

A best-effort LEXICAL check over the Bash command via the shared quote/redirect-aware tokenizer (_lex_command), ALLOW-WITH-A-NOTE by design (NO-ASK posture: it never returns an ask and never denies on a finding; read every ASK/ASKS below as that allow-with-informational-note outcome, an ambient-binding convention rather than a hazard; the EN-9 lesson: an open shell grammar has an irreducible undecidable tail, so no finding here denies; only the shared missing-tool_name contract denies). SCOPE ALIGNMENT with the rule text: expbnd keeps prefer-the-explicit-binding as a PRINCIPLE and makes the MECHANICAL requirement MANDATORY only in the ambient-target-CONFUSION cases (a directory change PRECEDING a git mutation, a wrapper that redirects git, or a breadth sweep that a relocation PRECEDES or that PRECEDES a publish (push)); this control matches that scope and does NOT and deliberately should NOT ASK on every bare ambient git. It fires on exactly TWO patterns, both ORDER-SENSITIVE (a shift confuses a git mutation OR a breadth op it PRECEDES; a breadth op is ADDITIONALLY a hazard when it PRECEDES a git push): (A) a cd/pushd/popd segment EARLIER in the SAME command feeding a later recognized mutating git subcommand that carries no ABSOLUTE explicit binding (a trailing shift, e.g. 'git commit && cd /x', does not confuse the earlier mutation and ALLOWS), and (B) a whole-tree breadth stage (git add -A/--all/'.'/':/'; git commit -a/--all/-am) that FOLLOWS a cd/pushd/popd shift OR PRECEDES a git push ('git add -A && cd /x' ALLOWS -- staging happened in the correct repo; 'git push && git add -A' ALLOWS -- the push published the pre-breadth state). DELIBERATE NON-FIRES, disclosed: a lone bare mutating git command in the session cwd (no cd, no push, no breadth) is ALLOWED, as is a lone 'git commit -am'/'git add -A' with no cd/push; the wrong-session-cwd residual is owned by confirm-execution-target (exetgt) at the reasoning layer and by git-discard (prsunc) for lossy verbs, and the lone-breadth sweep by separate-task-changes (septsk); asking on every bare git mutation would over-fire and train its own bypass. EXPLICIT-BINDING CREDIT: a binding is credited ONLY when it is an ABSOLUTE -C or an ABSOLUTE --git-dir; a RELATIVE -C/--git-dir still resolves against the ambient cwd and a lone --work-tree without --git-dir does not name which repository, so neither is a complete explicit binding and both route to the same ASK a bare ambient mutation would; even a credited absolute binding is NOT verified to point at the intended repository (absoluteness and explicitness are not intent, which stays exetgt's obligation). READ-ONLY EXEMPTIONS: the branch/tag mutation classifier is FAIL-SAFE / DEFAULT-MUTATING -- a git branch/tag command is treated as a MUTATION unless EVERY option token positively resolves to a recognized read-neutral role AND no create/rename/delete target is present (before or after the '--' end-of-options marker); it handles option abbreviations, attached-short values, optional-value flags, clustered shorts, and post-'--' targets, so unknown, ambiguous (non-unique prefix), or malformed forms resolve to mutating (this replaced an enumerate-the-reads design). The read cases are a filtered/verify LISTING ('git branch -l/--list', '--contains/--merged/--points-at', 'git tag -v/--verify') and a bare 'git branch'/'git tag' listing; likewise 'git branch --show-current', 'git tag --points-at', 'git config --get' or a bare 'git config <key>' read, and a bare 'git config' listing, are exempted even under a cd. Option recognition STOPS at a '--' end-of-options marker, so a file literally named '--all'/'-A' after '--' is an operand, not a breadth selector, while a genuine whole-tree pathspec ('.'/':/') still counts. WRAPPER HANDLING: the common BARE wrappers command/exec/builtin/env and a leading sudo ARE peeled, so 'command git ...', 'sudo git ...', and 'command cd ...' are judged like the bare form; a wrapper carrying its own option or assignment ('env -i', 'env FOO=1', 'sudo -u u') is a DISCLOSED residual left unpeeled (its option grammar is not guessed), as is any wrapper outside that set or one that fragments the git/cd command word. NOT CAUGHT (best-effort, not chased): an alias, shell function, eval, or fragmentation that removes a contiguous literal 'git' or cd/pushd command word; a cwd shift made in a PRIOR Bash call or via GIT_DIR=/GIT_WORK_TREE= environment (an inline GIT_DIR= assignment does NOT count as an explicit target, a disclosed conservative over-ask); a mutating subcommand outside the declared verb roster; plain (non-pruning) git fetch, deliberately excluded to hold the noise floor; mutations outside the Bash tool. A dynamic cd operand (cd "$D") still trips case A (the pattern, not the resolved dir, is judged). On a tokenizer parse failure a conservative raw scan ASKS on a visible cd+mutate or breadth+push pairing (which can over-ask on quoted prose inside the unparseable command) and otherwise allows; an unreadable command string ASKS; a missing tool_name denies (shared fail-closed contract). Overlaps by design (defence in depth, consistent ASK, never conflicting): abs-paths-bash also asks on a RELATIVE cd, git-discard also asks on a compound lossy discard, and git-stash-ref also notes on a relocated pop/apply (cd /x && git stash pop double-notes with this hook under the same expbnd rule). DEADLINE: main() gives this check 8 seconds (the 10-second hook timeout less 2), counted from before its payload read, and fails closed with exit 2 when it has not decided by then; on the worst shapes the hooks self-test times, up to 1 MB, its slowest call took about 0.36 s in-process on a 24-core host with Python 3.14.4 (2026-10-15). Interpreter start-up and a wait the interpreter cannot interrupt (a read from a hung mount, a long call into C code) fall outside that deadline, and whether the platform blocks a call whose hook it stops at its own timeout is unverified. Where SIGALRM, setitimer or the main thread is unavailable, or SIGALRM is blocked, the check runs with no deadline; cleanup that runs while the deadline unwinds is outside it.

A best-effort LEXICAL check over Bash commands via the shared quote/redirect-aware tokenizer and the git-explicit-binding wrapper peel. ALLOW-WITH-A-NOTE by design (NO-ASK): a recognized bare git stash pop/apply emits one informational systemMessage per command, with no permissionDecision; any positional operand silently allows. The manifest block default is the fail-closed handler-error class marker, not a blocking verdict on a bare stash operation.

PRESENCE IS NOT IDENTITY: no validation of well-formedness, existence, or intended entry; a SHA-shaped operand is not object validation, and stash@{N} can change referent between listing and execution. Dynamic operands, including "$REF" and command substitutions, count as explicit even if empty at runtime; an empty quoted operand also counts. This is the accepted under-warn direction. No automatic stash@{0} substitution and no recovery snapshot.

NOT RESOLVED: git aliases, shell aliases/functions, eval, unknown wrappers, and wrappers carrying their own options or assignments (env -i, env FOO=x, sudo -u u). The common BARE command/exec/builtin/env/sudo wrappers are peeled exactly as in git-explicit-binding. Simple quote fragments ARE decoded by the shared tokenizer; fragmentation or obfuscation that does not resolve to recognized command/verb tokens remains outside coverage. This targets accidental ambient binding, not an adversary. The shared segmenter splits ordinary separators (;, |, &&, ||, newlines) and (...) subshells but does NOT structurally parse {...} brace groups or shell control-flow constructs, so a bare pop/apply is missed only when an unpeeled brace or shell-keyword token occupies the command-word position of git's segment: for example a { group opener, or a control keyword such as if, elif, else, while, until, then, or do immediately preceding git in the same segment (these examples are illustrative, not exhaustive); a git stash pop that a ; or newline delimits into its own segment IS seen and warns (git_discard's generic fallback may still note the missed same-segment form); extending the shared segmenter to those forms is a family-wide follow-on.

SIBLING NOTES: this note can co-occur with git_discard's raw/pristine fallback note on a wrapped or compound pop/apply, and with git-explicit-binding's note on a relocated form (e.g. cd /x && git stash pop); such sibling notes are consistent, never conflicting.

OPTION-GRAMMAR PIN: the current pop/apply grammar has no value-taking options (-q/--quiet/--index). A future value-taking option can make its value read as an explicit operand and falsely allow; re-validate on git upgrade. Option validity itself is not checked.

STACK-BLIND: no git calls or filesystem probes. Every recognized bare pop/apply warns regardless of actual stack state, including a freshly created single-entry stack; conversely a dangerous stack receives no escalation. This accepted over-warning supports WARN rather than DENY. SURFACE BOUND: Bash PreToolUse only, with no resolution of prior-turn shell state. Other stash verbs, including bare git stash (push), are outside this guard; drop/clear/export belong to git_discard.

FAIL POSTURE: a tokenizer ValueError silently allows because unparsed text supplies no sound basis for this stash note. An absent/unreadable command emits the sibling's exact binding-convention note. Only the shared missing-tool_name contract returns a structured deny; an unexpected event hard-blocks and dispatcher errors retain the fail-closed manifest default.

DEADLINE: main() gives this check 8 seconds (the 10-second hook timeout less 2), counted from before its payload read, and fails closed with exit 2 when it has not decided by then; on the worst shapes the hooks self-test times, up to 1 MB, its slowest call took about 1.72 s in-process on a 24-core host with Python 3.14.4 (2026-10-15). Interpreter start-up and a wait the interpreter cannot interrupt (a read from a hung mount, a long call into C code) fall outside that deadline, and whether the platform blocks a call whose hook it stops at its own timeout is unverified. Where SIGALRM, setitimer or the main thread is unavailable, or SIGALRM is blocked, the check runs with no deadline; cleanup that runs while the deadline unwinds is outside it.

A RECORDING substrate, not an enforcement point: it appends launch rows (a Bash call with run_in_background true, or a registry-declared dispatch tool) and completion rows (a TaskOutput read) to the machine-written dispatch ledger the stop guard consumes as its Gap-B oracle. It never blocks; a failed ledger write is surfaced as a non-blocking systemMessage, never swallowed, and a lease max_age_hours horizon that cannot be evaluated does not turn this recorder off: the row is recorded anyway and the cannot-evaluate is surfaced as a note (armed and surfaced, never a silent skip). Coverage is exactly the hooked tools: a launch through an unhooked tool is invisible (costing one spurious stop-guard deny), a completion that never passes through TaskOutput is invisible until the staleness horizon expires the row, and the task-id extraction from tool responses is best-effort field matching. Both blind-spot directions are bounded by staleness plus the resume audit, and disclosed at the stop guard.

A subcommand, positional operand or option outside a listed form leaves the run outside the deny tier, and a separated option value that starts with - is read as a possible unlisted option.
